notes.title: Update – Revoked Game Keys
notes.content:
[h3]If you have encountered a problem with your House of Ashes Steam key being revoked,[b] please contact the reseller who sold you the key[/b]. We have provided [b]all official resellers with replacement keys[/b] for this purpose.

If you have already contacted your reseller and they were not able to send a replacement key, [b]please contact the [url=https://bnent.eu/TDPSupport]Bandai Namco Support Team[/url][/b].
 
We will ask you to send [b]the key that has been revoked plus a copy of your purchase invoice from the reseller[/b]  (most digital resellers will send an email invoice after purchase). With this information, our team will be able to issue a replacement key.
 
Our sincere apologies for this inconvenience. We thank you for your patience and hope that after this issue is resolved, you will continue to enjoy [i][b]The Dark Pictures: House of Ashes[/b][/i].[/h3]

This is a [b]mistake[/b] and we [b]apologise for the inconvenience[/b]. We are currently working to[b] resolve this issue as soon as possible[/b] in order to [b]restore access to all impacted players[/b]. We’ll keep you informed.

[h2]UPDATE OCT. 12th:[/h2]

[h3]Thank you for your patience during this investigation. 

We have communicated with [b]all official resellers of [i]House of Ashes[/i] to provide them with replacement keys[/b]. If you purchased your copy of House of Ashes from an official reseller, [b]please contact them for a replacement key[/b].

If you have already contacted your reseller and they were not able to send a replacement key, [b]please contact the [url=https://bnent.eu/TDPSupport]Bandai Namco Support Team[/url][/b].
 
We will ask you to send [b]the key that has been revoked plus a copy of your purchase invoice from the reseller[/b]  (most digital resellers will send an email invoice after purchase). With this information, our team will be able to issue a replacement key.
 
Our sincere apologies for this inconvenience. We thank you for your patience and hope that after this issue is resolved, you will continue to enjoy [i][b]The Dark Pictures: House of Ashes[/b][/i].[/h3]

Set in Iraq, 2003, in the shadows of the Zagros mountains, Special Forces are hunting for weapons of mass destruction when they are attacked. notes.title: Ask Me Anything with Supermassive Games 🧭
notes.content:
[h2]On September 15th, fans of The Dark Pictures Anthology were able to ask Will Doyle (Game Director) and Dom Ireland (Production Director) questions about House of Ashes during a Reddit AMA (Ask Me Anything).[/h2]
 

Here are the answers to some of the community’s most burning questions:

 
[h3]💬 [i]There are non-playable characters such as Merwin, Joey and Clarice who are savable and their lives have an effect on the story, an idea unique to House of Ashes, but how come, say, Jason and Nick are playable as opposed to Merwin or Clarice? (RedSon5)[/i][/h3]

We always want to have five playable characters. It’s a magic rule for us for the anthology! Our games are very much geared around that now. Those five are hooked into the relationships/traits system, and must adhere to the “everyone can live / everyone can die” rule. The NPCs can still be meaningful, but keeping them alive is usually only important for vital turns in the story (I sometimes think of them as keys, in that respect). Sometimes, we can force their deaths for dramatic effect, which is obviously something we can’t do with player characters. – Will Doyle


[h3]💬 [i]For House of Ashes, did you get to visit the locations for the setting? (Thatbrownmonster_)[/i][/h3]

Sadly not! But eagle-eyed fans who visit the British Museum in London will be able to see the real-life counterparts of several of our in-game objects! – Dom Ireland


[h3]💬 [i]Has the feedback on Little Hope's branching and story variation (or lack thereof) brought about any changes in House of Ashes' branching system and replayability? (_Ferret_)[/i][/h3]

Our games will always have different templates. Some may be much more variable, like Man of Medan, while others may be more streamlined, like Little Hope (and House of Ashes, to a degree). The important thing to stress is that there is no right answer here – really, it’s all down to the story. The story always wins. If we think a story deserves three distinct endings, we’ll try to make it happen. If it works better coming to a single, dramatic conclusion, we’ll do that instead. Obviously there are very important technical considerations — you only have so much butter to spread over your bread! — but we’re getting a lot better at planning and costing our games before committing, to ensure the best result. – Will Doyle


[h3]💬 [i]Will we get to learn more about the Curator and his background with each instalment? (CaptainMcSwan)[/i][/h3]

Yes, indeed, although it’s a slow burn! Each instalment introduces something new. We’ve learned that he has this vast collection of dark, sinister stories, with each story concerning life and death. He follows you, watching and observing, and his pictures offer hints about what might come. Why does he do this? He can’t determine the outcome of each story – that's your job - but he can offer hints. Is he even allowed to do that? We know he has rules, he’s part of some grand system, but he isn’t afraid to break these from time to time. Will this get him into trouble? Does he even care if it does? Keep an eye out for how House of Ashes hints at more. – Dom Ireland
 

[h3]💬 [i]Will we get any LGBT characters or a female majority? (KateDensonIsBae)[/i][/h3]

Yes, 100%, watch this space! We’re a very diverse studio and firmly believe that representation is important in our stories. We haven’t featured LGBTQ+ characters in the anthology so far, but future titles certainly will. – Dom Ireland
 

[h2]Hungry for more? [url=https://www.reddit.com/r/DarkPicturesAnthology/comments/pllm0b/were_the_supermassive_games_dev_team_ask_us/]Dig deeper into the AMA on Reddit[/url][/h2]
